1 idea · Investing

Why rising rates hit tech stocks hardest

A share is worth the profits it will earn in the future, discounted back to today. A higher interest rate means a bigger discount, and it grows the further away the profit is.

€100 in 10 years is worth €74 today at 3% but only €61 at 5%, a 17.5% drop. €100 in 1 year only falls 1.9%. Growth and AI companies earn most of their profit far in the future, so they fall more.

Higher rates cut the value of distant profits, so growth stocks swing harder.
